newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Body Shop profits up but US still slow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Body Shop profits up but US still slow.

text.p: Controversial green cosmetic retailer Body Shop International reported a 30 percent profit rise on Thursday, driven by dynamic growth in Asia, but losses deepened in the U.S., where it expects only gradual improvement.
Pretax profits for the six months to August 31 rose to 11.8 million pounds ($19.2 million) from 9.1 million. The dividend payout rose 39 percent to 1.5 pence.
Total sales were up 11 percent to 117.1 million pounds, while retail sales grew 13 percent to 275.5 million.
Chairman Gordon Roddick said there was "strong growth in Asian markets and regeneration in Australia". But he added the United States had seen a slowdown, producing a bigger loss.
There were fewer new stores in Europe and sales in Britain were sluggish, moving up by just one percent.

In Asia profits rose more than 40 percent to 6.5 million pounds and the region accounted for roughly half of the 63 new shops opened in the first half year. This included Body Shop's first two outlets in the Philippines. It plans to open in Korea in the second half.
Body Shop's shares rose four pence to 199-1/2 pence.

Chief executive Anita Roddick, the group's guiding light, has had a turbulent relationship with the investment community and considered taking Body Shop private but then abandoned the idea. Husband Gordon Roddick said it was certainly not something the group was still looking into.
The retailer, which campaigns on green and social issues, has expanded from a single shop in 1976 to a global empire of nearly 1,436 stores in 46 countries.
It has seen sales power ahead in key Far East markets but has struggled to make a success of its stores in the fiercely competitive U.S. retail market, while growth in its home market has stagnated.
Roddick said sales in the United States were improving but it was a slow process.
"I think what we have is a long, slow, gradual improvement," he told Reuters in a telephone interview. "We're still looking towards a long term success in the USA."

The firm's losses in the United States rose to 3.4 million pounds from 2.4 million a year ago. But a decline in sales, based on a comparable number of stores, slowed to four percent from eight percent in the same half last year.

Last year Body Shop launched a U.S. marketing campaign to raise its profile. It has just recruited a new U.S. chief executive, Steen Kanter, who worked for Swedish furniture retailer IKEA, where he was behind an uplift in its U.S. performance.
In Britain, Roddick said people were spending a bit more money in the shops, with the average transaction up by about five percent from just under five pounds.

The group is trying to broaden its appeal and has introduced a new skin care range aimed at women in their thirties. It is redesigning its stores and has a trial format in its store near London's Oxford Circus which has done away with its trademark green colour scheme. ($1=.6141 Pound)
